facts.audience: Orange County residents on time-of-use electricity plans
facts.problem: Home AC runs during the peak-price window on the timeline
facts.cause: Cooling activity overlaps the expensive peak hours on a time-of-use plan
facts.solution: Pre-cool the home before the peak window, then raise the thermostat slightly during peak hours
facts.outcome: Some cooling shifts away from expensive hours; check your plan's peak times

checks: Narration used word for word, split in order across three chapters
Every fact comes from the brief: no rates, times of day, numbers, savings or guarantees
No digits and no forbidden words (save, guarantee, always, never, best, lowest)
Only house, AC unit, thermostat and timeline are used; no underground cutaway or shield
Four objects: house (2x1) and timeline (3x1) are large, AC and thermostat are 1x1
No overlaps: house r1c1-r1c2, AC r1c3, thermostat r2c1, timeline r3c1-r3c3
Thermostat callout has free neighbouring cell r2c2
AC sits next to the house so the pre-cooling link is short
Every object is drawn before it is changed or connected; thermostat is drawn at start of chapter three
Each event word appears in that chapter's narration
Text limits: labels <=14, kickers <=28, headline lines <=20, callout and link labels <=22, gauge <=30, checklist <=34
Chapter order: problem (peak overlap), change (pre-cooling, shift earlier), fix and outcome (thermostat up, less peak activity, check plan)
supplied_narration: On a time-of-use plan? Cool your home before peak rates, then raise the thermostat a little. That can shift some cooling away from expensive hours. Check your plan's peak times.
